guides.title: Big Agnes Copper Spur Models Compared — UL1, UL2, UL3, Bikepack & XL
guides.description: Compare eight current Big Agnes Copper Spur models by capacity, representative catalog weight, official reference price and intended use.
guides.eyebrow: Manually reviewed Copper Spur range guide

related_guides.label: Compare the full Big Agnes Tiger Wall range

guides.intro: The current Copper Spur range shares a three-season, freestanding HyperBead platform, but capacity is only the first decision. Standard models minimize carry weight, Bikepack versions add short poles and bike-mounting storage, and XL versions trade a modest weight and price increase for more room.
guides.verdict: For one backpacker, start with the standard UL1; for two people or a solo camper who values room, the standard UL2 is the most balanced choice; for two people who want extra length and headroom, choose the UL2 XL. Move to a Bikepack model only when its 12-inch pole set and bike-mounting dry bag solve a real packing problem. The UL3 and UL3 XL make the most sense for three sleepers or a roomy two-person setup.
takeaways: Capacity first: UL1, UL2 and UL3 are the one-, two- and three-person branches. A couple should compare UL2 with UL2 XL; a roomy pair should also consider UL3.

Standard models: the representative catalog weights rise from about 0.97 kg for UL1 to 1.19 kg for UL2 and 1.59 kg for UL3. These are the lightest choices at each listed capacity in this eight-model set.

Bikepack trade-off: Bikepack versions add about 390 g, 480 g and 370 g over the corresponding standard UL1, UL2 and UL3 records. In return, Big Agnes lists a 12-inch Shortstik pole set, waterproof dry-bag stuff sack and bike-mounting features.
XL trade-off: UL2 XL adds about 90 g and $50 over UL2; UL3 XL adds about 30 g and $50 over UL3. Big Agnes positions XL around extra length, width and head height rather than a different capacity.

Reference prices: the reviewed official prices run from $499.95 for UL1 to $699.95 for UL3 Bikepack and UL3 XL. Price alone should not decide between standard, Bikepack and XL because each solves a different packing or space need.
Shared platform: all eight official listings describe a three-season, fully freestanding Copper Spur design using HyperBead fabric.
guides.limitations: This is a specification-based buying guide, not a hands-on durability or weather test. Weight values are representative normalized catalog values in our official-source dataset; Big Agnes may separately publish packed, trail or component weights, so do not treat these figures as interchangeable. Prices and availability were checked on 2026-08-03 and can change by market or promotion. The guide covers the current standard UL1/UL2/UL3, Bikepack and XL branches; it intentionally excludes older HV records, mtnGLO variants and larger UL4/UL5 models.

guides.title: Big Agnes Tiger Wall Models Compared — Platinum, UL & Bikepack
guides.description: Compare eight Big Agnes Tiger Wall models by capacity, representative catalog weight, semi-freestanding architecture, official price and intended use.
guides.eyebrow: Manually reviewed Tiger Wall range guide

related_guides.label: Compare the full Big Agnes Copper Spur range
Tiger Wall UL2 vs Copper Spur UL2

guides.intro: Tiger Wall is a three-season, semi-freestanding tent family built around low weight and side entry. Capacity identifies sleeping space; Platinum, standard UL and Bikepack identify different materials, feature sets and packing priorities. Those choices should be compared within the same capacity before treating any weight difference as meaningful.
guides.verdict: Choose the standard UL1, UL2 or UL3 as the default backpacking option for the capacity you need. Pay for Platinum only when its lighter 7D fabric and stripped-back fast-and-light design matter more than price; the representative UL2 and Tiger Wall 2 Platinum records both weigh about 0.99 kg, so the Platinum name alone does not guarantee a lower comparable total. Choose Bikepack only when the 12-inch pole set, waterproof mounting sack and bike storage features solve a real packing problem.
takeaways: Capacity is not a performance tier: UL1 is the one-person branch, while UL2/Platinum 2 and UL3/Platinum 3 are the two- and three-person branches. A larger number describes space, not automatic weather strength or overall quality.
Standard UL baseline: representative catalog weights are about 0.85 kg for UL1, 0.99 kg for UL2 and 1.19 kg for UL3, with reviewed official prices of $469.95, $499.95 and $579.95.

Platinum trade-off: Tiger Wall 2 Platinum and UL2 both normalize to about 0.99 kg in this catalog, while Platinum costs $200 more. Tiger Wall 3 Platinum is about 80 g lighter than UL3 but costs $170 more. Platinum uses lighter 7D HyperBead fabric and a reduced feature set; it is not a capacity upgrade.

Current Bikepack trade-off: UL1 Bikepack adds about 340 g and $30 over UL1; UL2 Bikepack adds about 370 g and $50 over UL2. Big Agnes lists a 12-inch Shortstik pole set, waterproof dry-bag stuff sack and bike-mounting loops as the reason to choose them.

UL3 Bikepack warning: the listed UL3 Bikepack Solution Dye record is an older, separate solution-dyed model at a temporary $467.45 sale price. Its 1.5 kg representative weight and discount should not be used as the normal price trend for the current UL1/UL2 Bikepack range.

Shared architecture: Big Agnes describes the reviewed Tiger Wall models as three-season and semi-freestanding. Capacity and material changes do not establish stronger wind or rain performance without a separate test.
guides.limitations: This is a specification-based selection guide, not a hands-on weather, durability or livability test. Weights are representative normalized catalog values and may not use the same packed, trail or minimum basis shown elsewhere by the manufacturer. Prices and availability were checked on 2026-08-03 and can change. The UL3 Bikepack Solution Dye is retained for completeness but is an older sale record, not evidence of current-series pricing. Interior dimensions and capacity labels are not used here to infer stability, comfort or performance.

guides.title: Montbell Down Hugger 650 Models Compared — #2 vs #3 vs #5
guides.description: Compare six Montbell Down Hugger 650 sleeping bags by official ISO comfort and lower-limit temperatures, Regular or Long fit, packed weight and UK price.
guides.eyebrow: Manually reviewed Down Hugger 650 range guide
guides.intro: Down Hugger 650 model numbers identify temperature tiers, not capacity. In this UK range, #2 is the warmest option, #3 sits in the middle and #5 targets milder nights. Each tier has a Regular and Long version with the same published temperature ratings but different fit, packed weight and price.
guides.verdict: Start with the official comfort temperature: choose #5 for mild nights around 8°C, #3 for cooler three-season use around 3°C, or #2 when a -1°C comfort rating is the appropriate planning point. Choose Long only if you need its 198 cm maximum occupant height instead of the Regular model's 183 cm fit; Long adds about 80–120 g and £10–£25 without changing the published temperature rating.
takeaways: How to choose a temperature tier: use the official comfort figure as the more conservative first planning point. Do not treat the lower-limit figure as a routine comfort target, and leave margin for your sleep system and conditions.
#2: Regular and Long are both listed at -1°C comfort and -7°C lower limit. Packed weights are about 0.93 kg and 1.05 kg, with £310 and £335 reference prices.
#3: both lengths are listed at 3°C comfort and -2°C lower limit. Packed weights are about 0.72 kg and 0.82 kg, with £265 and £275 reference prices.
#5: both lengths are listed at 8°C comfort and 3°C lower limit. Packed weights are about 0.60 kg and 0.68 kg, with £220 and £230 reference prices.
Regular vs Long: Montbell lists maximum occupant heights of 183 cm for Regular and 198 cm for Long. The size suffix changes fit, weight and price, not the published temperature tier.

Temperature evidence: Montbell UK labels these comfort and lower-limit values as ISO tested. CampGear Compare links every product page but has not independently reviewed a laboratory report or performed its own thermal test.
guides.limitations: This is a specification-based selection guide, not an independent warmth test. Montbell UK labels the published comfort and lower-limit temperatures as ISO tested, but CampGear Compare has not independently verified the laboratory reports. Individual warmth varies with shelter, sleeping pad, clothing, humidity, wind, physiology and other conditions. Packed weights include the stuff bag and are rounded to the catalog's kilogram display. Prices and availability were checked on 2026-08-04 in the UK market; the Regular #3 listing was sold out at review time, and all stock and prices can change.

guides.title: Big Agnes Tiger Wall UL2 vs Copper Spur UL2
guides.description: Compare Big Agnes Tiger Wall UL2 and Copper Spur UL2 by representative weight, architecture, official positioning and price.
guides.intro: These two-person Big Agnes tents trade minimum listed weight against structure and feature level. Tiger Wall targets minimalists; Copper Spur emphasizes a freestanding, roomier platform.
takeaways: Weight: Tiger Wall UL2 is listed around 0.99 kg versus 1.19 kg for Copper Spur UL2.
Architecture: Tiger Wall uses a lightweight single-pole architecture; Copper Spur is described as fully freestanding.
Price: Tiger Wall UL2 currently starts about $100 below Copper Spur UL2.
Shared material: both current listings highlight Big Agnes HyperBead fabric.
Decision: prioritize Tiger Wall for the lower representative weight; prioritize Copper Spur when freestanding structure and interior comfort matter more.

guides.title: NEMO Hornet vs Dragonfly vs Dagger OSMO
guides.description: Compare NEMO Hornet, Dragonfly and Dagger OSMO backpacking tents by official positioning, structure and current reference price.
guides.intro: Hornet, Dragonfly and Dagger represent three different priorities in NEMO's backpacking line: minimum weight, balanced freestanding space, and maximum livability.
takeaways: Hornet: NEMO positions it as the ultralight option, using a minimal pole structure and Flybar for added volume.
Dragonfly: the listing emphasizes a freestanding frame and balance between weight and livability.
Dagger: NEMO describes it as the roomiest, most livable backpacking option of the three.
Price: current ranges overlap by capacity; verify the exact person-count variant before comparing totals.
Data limitation: the current catalog lacks normalized weights for these multi-variant listings, so this page does not invent a single figure.

guides.title: Therm-a-Rest NeoAir XLite vs XTherm NXT
guides.description: Compare Therm-a-Rest NeoAir XLite NXT and XTherm NXT sleeping pads by representative weight, official positioning and reference price.
guides.intro: XLite NXT is the lighter all-season model, while XTherm NXT is positioned around maximum warmth-to-weight performance for colder use.
takeaways: Weight: representative catalog weights are about 0.33 kg for XLite NXT and 0.44 kg for XTherm NXT.
Positioning: Therm-a-Rest calls XLite an all-season do-it-all pad and XTherm its warmth-to-weight specialist.
Price: XTherm NXT currently starts about $50 above XLite NXT.
Shape: compare these standard models separately from the wider rectangular MAX variants.
Decision: choose by expected overnight temperatures first, then compare the 110 g representative weight difference.
